Shocker!! Someone doesn't want to recommend a product. I’ll explain why. This game costs more than it should even when on sale. I got it at 50% off (~$27.00 USD), which felt like a great deal until I actually started playing.
The trailers do a great job of pulling you in, but the actual gameplay is a hollow sandbox. There is zero narrative urgency. It suffers from the "Fallout 4 condition"—your siblings are captured, yet there is no threat of them dying, no clock ticking, and absolutely nothing pushing you forward except a checklist to grow your clan. You can play board games, trade, or do tournaments forever, but it quickly devolves into a meaningless grind. Eventually, you hit a wall where the game forces you to level up troops, but the economic loop doesn't cover your party's upkeep. To make it worse, defeating groups of looters yields garbage loot. Even when they have strong leaders, they rarely drop gear you can actually use or pass to a companion.
The combat is incredibly wonky and lacks intuition. There is a noticeable input lag, and using polearms is an absolute chore. Charging down a peasant with a spear shouldn't be a guessing game of spacing, and the supposed target lock system is practically non-existent. It’s worse than Kingdom Come: Deliverance—which is vastly more complex but equally unsatisfying.
Finally, the world feels dead. Interacting with NPCs is awful because everyone shares the exact same dialogue tree. Once you've seen it once, you just blindly click through the text to dump quests into your journal.
I know a small team made this, but a lot of it is incredibly rough. They claim this game is out of beta. Personally? I think they're lying. Skip this unless you love paying premium prices for an unfinished, repetitive grind.

Conditional recommend.

This game has the most unpleasant melee combat system I have ever seen. It's a sort of directional blocking where the direction you need to block is based not on where the attack is coming from visually but what type of attack it is. So for example you must look down and press block to block a thrust attack that visually is coming from up and left on the screen (someone standing in front of you). It would have been so much more intuitive to press block and then sweep across the path of the attack, but instead they have this weird jank system that feels like it was invented from scratch by someone who never played a game before.

There are also some other oddities like the player being the only character in the game who can use the secondary kick skill that throws an opponent briefly off balance.

The good news is your personal impact in melee battles is just not that great in the first place, so you can avoid that entirely if you hate it as intensely as I do. There is no healing in combat so ranged weapons that let you avoid damage and headshot people throughout the fight are a much better investment of player time, or you can just order troops around and forego combat entirely (but you may as well shoot someone).

My other main complaint is that the skill system is sort of opaque (actually everything in this game is opaque: it doesn't explain itself, and half the time you can't even find it on a wiki, so you're looking at years old outdated forum posts instead). This has had the effect of making me abandon my first few runs as I find out things I was trying are actually bad and unfixable. You can respec only one of the three types of thing you select as you level up, so as you learn how they work, you realize you've stunted this character's useful progress for life.



Bearing all that in mind, it's otherwise a decent sandbox game where you spend most of your time in a CK-like map view and then transition into 3D environments to fight or talk at people. You can be a mercenary, bandit, trader, landowner, all of the above, and so on. Runs pretty well at max settings even on my now 5-6 years old pc.

Bannerlord is a worthy continuation of an incredible series that has been with me since childhood. Playing it brings back the nostalgia and memories of all those great moments I had with the previous games, while still feeling like a bigger and more modern Mount & Blade. Some games are simply more than games, and this series is one of them for me.

Early Access game in disguise — mods carry this game but there are some things even mods can't fix. Instead of polishing mechanics, fixing base game issues and adding essential features (that the predecessor Warband had), release a DLC instead which itself should've been part of the final game.

The stealth tutorial in Mount & Blade II: Bannerlord is an unadulterated piece of trash.

It is a miserable, broken chore forced into an engine that was never built for it.
This isn't Assassin's Creed.

Nobody buys a medieval sandbox simulator about massive cavalry charges and castle sieges to play a half-baked, clunky crouching simulator.

Worst of all, it's a blatant scam.

The unforgiving, trial-and-error design forces you to replay the exact same sequence so many times that it completely drains your two-hour Steam refund window.

You spend your entire trial period trapped in a loading-screen simulator instead of playing the game you actually paid for.

The guards have psychic vision through walls, the body-dragging physics are completely broken, and a single mistake forces a full restart. It is a masterclass in horrific game design that traps your money and wastes your time.

This is a game to which I always come back to once in a while. It has theoretically endless possibilities with mods, and honestly cheers for all the modders out there, they make everything so much better. You can play in the universe of Game of Thrones, Lord of The Rings, you can play on maps like Europe and so on and there's also tons of gameplay changing mods which can make the game totally different from what vanilla is. 

For the first playthrough I would recommend to play vanilla to get a feel for how the game is, but after that? Go nuts with the mods, because they make next playthroughs memorable. 

It's also fun in the way that you can play it in so many different ways. You can either make your troops simply charge and forget about any strategic or tactical thought and fight in the thick of it. Or you can play as an army general, who stays in the back and commands his units. You can even forget about all the combat and go for a full merchant run where you trade constantly and create an economical powerhouse. You can play as a bandit lord. And so on, and so forth.

Bannerlord II is a sensational game, you start as a lowly one man on a mission to do some sandbox shenanigans. The base game is very fun for 2-3 playthroughs. However, it gets repetitive VERY quickly. The wider community offers a wide range of experiences from PvP to total conversion mods that make the game reach its full potential. Mount and Blade III in 10 years better have coop on release or I WILL burn down a Wendy's in my underwear.

8/10 Would Recommend

 Mostly, its manageable, working best when you issue ALL the orders. If you turn on the AI sgts to control certain aspects, Its likely to bite you in the bum at the worst time. I dunno why its so terrible in the sieges specifically, but my word, can it be frustrating when you have stormed the wall, got a foot hold, and your troops just stop climbing the ladders or the tower. 

Otherwise Id give this game a solid 7. Its a hardcore battle sim/empire builder. Dont expect it to be easy, even on the easiest settings. 依旧是人均超人的卡拉迪亚

如果要选一款承载我整个童年游戏情怀的作品，那一定是《骑马与砍杀2：霸主》。对我而言，它从来不止是一款冷兵器战争游戏，更是藏在年少时光里，迟迟未曾圆满的执念与梦想。

第一次接触骑砍系列，是小时候趴在哥哥身后看他游玩的午后。彼时的我年纪尚小，看不懂复杂的兵种调配、阵营博弈，却深深被屏幕里的中世纪世界吸引。看着哥哥策马扬鞭、领兵冲锋，带着小队士兵征战旷野、坚守城池，从零开始积累财富、收服将士、纵横列国，那种自由热血的乱世江湖，在我心里种下了深深的种子。

那时候只能静静观望，满心羡慕却无从体验。看着卡拉迪亚大陆的辽阔原野、林立城邦，看着沙场之上刀光剑影、千军奔腾，我悄悄许下心愿，长大后一定要亲自踏入这片世界，圆自己的骑士梦想。这份纯粹的热爱，陪伴我度过了漫长童年，也让我一直默默期待着续作的到来。

时隔多年，我终于如愿上手《骑马与砍杀2》，儿时的遗憾终于圆满。相较于前作，二代的画面、动作、机制全面升级，却完整保留了系列最核心的自由与真实。没有固化的剧情束缚，没有强制的任务枷锁，开局孤身一人、一马一剑，所有传奇都由自己亲手书写，这正是骑砍最动人的魅力。

游戏的美好，藏在每一处真实的细节里。从招募第一位伙伴、组建第一支小队，到征战沙场、割据一方；从游走贸易积攒资本，到攻城略地、建立属于自己的势力，每一步成长都踏实又滚烫。真实的冷兵器格斗、拟真的战马冲锋、灵活的兵种搭配，让每一场战斗都极具沉浸感，每一次胜利都让人热血沸腾。

更让我心动的是，这款游戏有着无限的可玩性。丰富的模组生态让游戏永葆新鲜，无论是复刻经典剧情，还是解锁全新乱世玩法，都能带来截然不同的游戏体验。简单易懂的底层逻辑，深度十足的策略玩法，既能轻松休闲闯荡江湖，也能深耕战术逐鹿天下，适配每一位玩家的节奏。

多年过去，当初趴在屏幕前憧憬乱世的小孩，终于能亲自策马驰骋在这片热爱的大陆。《骑马与砍杀2》于我而言，早已超越游戏本身。它承载着童年的美好回忆，兑现了年少的满心期许。在这里，我终于完成了儿时的梦想，身披铠甲、手握长枪，在属于自己的乱世里，奔赴一场永不落幕的沙场征途。
一辈子也要玩一次的游戏

[h1] 绝对值得一试 [/h1]骑砍2于我而言不仅是一款断断续续玩了上百小时的游戏，更代表着一段无忧无虑的时光。在以往的测评中，我最多看到的是[strike] “无代餐” [/strike]的说法，但这种泛泛的描述显然是缺少推荐的诚意且放在绝大多数的游戏上显然都能适用。说了些不相干的，回到游戏上来，骑砍不完全是必须精打细算每一步，一子落错满盘皆输的运营游戏，也不完全是胜负就在一念之间的硬核格斗游戏，同样也不完全是一款让你坐镇中军，让你对你的每一名士兵如指臂使的即时战略，但正式这种夹杂着动作、战术、王国动态的多面一体的体验，让他成为一款可以在一段时间内，让你消磨数个小时的优先之选。当然，游戏不可能适合每一个人的口味，但总体而言，这是一款没那么难上手，却又可以从多个维度给你带来正向反馈的作品，仅凭这点，就足以吸引你来到[i] 卡拉迪亚 [/i]，并享受一段[i] 霸主 [/i]之旅。
